title: Ben Johnson discusses Mike Ditka's impact on Bears | Press Conference
headline: Kyle Monangai is out this week with a toe injury and is week to week (not an IR candidate). Roschon Johnson steps into a bigger role, and D'Andre Swift is expected to play and may see a larger workload against the Packers. Caleb Williams is still working back from a hamstring injury.
summary: Johnson opened by paying tribute to Mike Ditka, who died the morning of the press conference, calling him the gold standard for the franchise. On injuries, Kyle Monangai's toe issue turned out to be more serious than the thumb problem the team had been watching. He is in a boot, seeing a specialist, will not play this week, and is week to week but not an IR candidate. Everything else is trending the right way for availability. The coach said a practice window player will likely be elevated to the 53 now that a roster spot is open. Roschon Johnson drew praise as a complete back who runs hard, catches well, and pass protects, so he is positioned for a bigger role. Swift is the same guy, was a full participant on Thursday, and Johnson is optimistic he will help on Sunday. When asked about a 75/25 workload split, Johnson said "Maybe". Caleb Williams is recovering from a hamstring injury, has started a throwing progression, and has no setbacks so far, but there is no timeline. Red zone and finishing drives remain the team's top offensive problem. Grady Jarrett is playing at a higher level than last year, flashing his Atlanta form.

injuries.detail: Toe injury is worse than expected. He is in a boot, seeing a specialist, and will not practice or play this week. He is week to week, not an IR candidate, and the thumb was the initially known issue.
Recovering from a hamstring injury. He was throwing a little a few days ago and is on a running and throwing progression with no setbacks, but there is no return timeline.
Dealing with an unspecified issue like most players who have played all four games. He practiced Thursday and is expected to help on Sunday.

signals.claim: Monangai will miss this week's game against the Packers and is week to week with the toe injury.
signals.note: Starting-caliber RB out with an unknown timeline, so drop his fantasy value until there is clarity and plan around a multi-week absence.
signals.quote: turns out the toe is a bigger deal than we initially anticipated.

signals.claim: Roschon Johnson will take on a bigger role in the backfield with Monangai out.
signals.note: Described as a complete back with size, receiving ability and pass-protection value, which makes him a short-term RB add or flex consideration.
signals.quote: he can do a little bit of everything which we really value at that spot.

signals.claim: Swift may see a larger share of the carries this week, possibly a 75/25 split, and is expected to play.
signals.note: With Monangai out, Swift is the likely lead back if healthy, but the coach only said "maybe" about the workload split.

signals.claim: Williams will continue the hamstring throwing progression with no set return date.
signals.note: Quarterback timeline is uncertain, which matters for all Bears pass-catchers, and the backup is likely to start in the meantime.

signals.claim: Jarrett is playing at a higher level than last year and is a leader of the defensive line.
signals.note: Positive for IDP and Bears defensive-line performance.
signals.quote: he's playing at a higher level this year than what, what he showed last year.

topics.detail: Johnson honored Ditka as a legend of the franchise as both a player and a coach and said he feels humbled to sit in the same chair. He said he never met him and plans to talk to the team about Ditka.
Finishing drives has been a problem for three weeks. Johnson says there is no single fix, only more awareness, clear play calls and execution, and he wanted another good red zone practice on Friday.
Several players are deep into their practice windows. Johnson said it is highly likely one will be elevated to the 53 now that a spot is open, but he did not say who.
The team spent the start of the week discussing the history with Green Bay. Johnson sees the game as a chance to write another chapter in the rivalry.

title: Jim Harbaugh Remembers Mike Ditka & Gives Injury Updates
headline: Little actionable news: Rashawn Slater had successful surgery, and Quentin Johnston's chest injury was confirmed but his Sunday availability is unclear.
summary: Most of the press conference was Harbaugh's tribute to Mike Ditka, who had just died. He offered condolences to Ditka's family and the city of Chicago and called him an American original and a true competitor. He described Ditka as a man of faith, family and football, and said he loved playing for him. He shared a story about watching Ditka write $500 checks to strangers who had sent letters asking for help. On football, a reporter asked whether the offensive line group that finished the last game would be the same five players, perhaps in different positions. Harbaugh said Sunday's game would show how the line is deployed, and that the previous game was a 'sneak peek.' He hadn't spoken to Rashawn Slater since right before surgery but understood it was successful. The reporter's question about Quentin Johnston's chest injury drew only 'Yes, yes,' and the transcript doesn't make clear whether that confirms he got hurt in the game or that he will play Sunday. No other injury, depth chart or usage details were given.

injuries.detail: Had surgery and Harbaugh understands it was successful. No return timeline or injury type was given in this transcript.

A reporter asked about his chest injury and whether it was in the game on Sunday. Harbaugh said 'Yes, yes,' which is ambiguous between the injury happening in the last game and him playing this Sunday.

signals.claim: Slater has had surgery that went successfully; Harbaugh gave no return date.
signals.note: A key offensive tackle is recovering from surgery, so the line behind Justin Herbert and the run game may be reshuffled.
signals.quote: understand that it was a successful surgery.

signals.claim: Johnston has a chest injury, and Harbaugh confirmed a question about it relating to Sunday's game.
signals.note: His availability against Denver is unclear, so check the final injury report before setting lineups.

topics.detail: Harbaugh paid tribute to Ditka after his passing. He praised his faith, generosity and competitiveness and shared a story about Ditka quietly writing checks to people in need.
Harbaugh said the five-man group that finished the last game, perhaps in different positions, previews the line. He said Sunday would show how the line is deployed.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 9, 2026
headline: Eagles trade C Cam Jurgens and Lane Johnson retires, so Drew Kendall, Jake Majors and Willie Lampkin step into the interior line. Goedert is back at practice and Wicks should be fine.
summary: Sirianni said the team had a good week of preparation and has "locked arms" after trading Cam Jurgens and the Lane Johnson retirement. He praised Jurgens warmly, said he was on board with the move, and said he feels confident in the interior line group. He said the game plan will still lean on what the team does best and its core system, and that the young linemen have taken plenty of reps in it. He singled out Jake Majors and Willie Lampkin as having great camps and good preseason showings, and he said Drew Kendall has been solid, keeps improving, and can get the line on the same page. Dallas Goedert was back at practice and looked good. Dontayvion Wicks showed up on the practice report, but Sirianni expects him to practice and called him tough. Sirianni said the team is looking into the number of soft-tissue injuries this year. He said he's excited about Dameon Pierce's opportunity after the elevation. He called Jacksonville a well-coached team that leads the league in turnover differential, with Trevor Lawrence playing well and Parker Washington dangerous on special teams. He did not embrace the underdog framing and spoke more broadly about leaning on teammates in adversity.

injuries.detail: Back on the practice field this week and looked pretty good, with one more practice still to come.
Appeared on the practice report; Sirianni anticipates him practicing today but will see where he is at the end of the day. The nature of the injury was not stated.

signals.claim: Will keep playing a central role on the interior line and help set protections and communication.
signals.note: With Jurgens gone, Kendall's intelligence and growth make him a key piece for the line that protects Hurts and opens holes for Barkley.

signals.claim: Is expected to be involved on the interior line against Jacksonville.
signals.note: He may see real snaps with the line shorthanded, which matters for run-blocking and pass-protection outlooks.
signals.quote: there's a reason, you know, Jake's here.

signals.claim: Is in the mix to play on the interior line after a strong camp and preseason.
signals.note: Another young lineman who could start or rotate in, which adds some uncertainty to the line's performance.
signals.quote: both of them had great camps.

signals.claim: Goedert is back practicing and is on track to return.
signals.note: A returning starting tight end boosts Philadelphia's passing-game options, though his Sunday status is not yet confirmed.
signals.quote: I thought he had a nice week of practice.

signals.claim: Wicks is expected to practice Friday, but his status will be clearer after that.
signals.note: He has produced well, so check the final injury report before Sunday.
signals.quote: anticipating him being out there today.

signals.claim: Pierce has been elevated and will have an opportunity to contribute at running back.
signals.note: Sirianni praised him, but gave no usage details, so any role is likely small behind Saquon Barkley.

topics.topic: Cam Jurgens trade and Lane Johnson retirement
topics.detail: Sirianni was on board with trading Jurgens, praised his toughness, and said there is no message change after Lane Johnson's retirement. He said the focus is getting back to work.

topics.topic: Game planning for the offensive line
topics.detail: The team will do what its players do best within its core system and will adjust to whoever plays. The young linemen have taken many system reps since training camp.
The team has had more soft-tissue injuries than in the past and is looking into it. Sirianni said they must balance practicing with managing players over a long season.
Sirianni called the Jaguars a well-coached, tackling-focused team that leads the league in turnover differential. He praised Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington on special teams.
He did not say the team is embracing the underdog role. He said teams should lock arms and lean on each other through adversity.

title: Todd Bowles: Zyon McCollum ‘Playing Like An All-Pro’ | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield (hand/splint) is still not cleared, and the Bucs plan to start Jalon Daniels vs. the Steelers; Bucky Irving is the hot-hand back in a run-first offense.
summary: Bowles praised Bucky Irving for bringing a different energy and a huge spark, with a 72-yard run and a game-closing 22-yard run behind a hard-working offensive line. He said the team is planning to start Jalon Daniels against the Steelers, with Baker Mayfield's hand still in a smaller splint and more to be known when he comes in. Daniels was praised for playing smart and decisive, knowing when to run, and handling the huddle after a short-week prep. Bowles called the run game "kind of who we are" and said it fuels complementary football. Zyon McCollum was lauded as playing like an all-pro corner thanks to better film study and recognition, and Jacob Parrish also got credit despite a brief breather when he tired. Rueben Bain returned from a missed-games absence and looked good with some rust, while the pass rush (including David Walker) generated the best pressure of the year without sacks. Sean Tucker was described as the third back who gets only a few snaps unless he is the hot hand, and Bowles took blame for going for it on 4th-and-goal instead of kicking a field goal. He also flagged growing offensive line penalties as something to clean up.

injuries.detail: Hand injury with a smaller splint; Bowles will know more when he comes in, but the team is planning to start Jalon Daniels vs. the Steelers.
Returned to action after missing a couple of games; looked good, needs to knock off some technique rust.

signals.claim: Jalon Daniels will start at QB against the Steelers.
signals.note: Daniels is the expected starter again in Week 7 while Mayfield's hand heals, so his QB and offense stock is relevant for streaming and stacking.
signals.quote: right now we're planning on starting Jaylen against the Steelers.

signals.claim: Mayfield will not start against the Steelers unless his hand improves; Bowles will know more when he returns to the facility.
signals.note: Mayfield is a risk to miss Week 7, so fantasy managers should have a backup plan.
signals.quote: He's got a smaller grip on it. I'll know more when he comes in.

signals.claim: Irving will keep the lead role as long as he stays the hot hand in a run-first approach.
signals.note: He produced explosive runs and a spark, and Bowles said there was no denying keeping him in the game.
signals.quote: Bucky brought a different energy in this game.

signals.claim: Tucker will get only about 3-7 plays per game as the third back, varying by who is hot.
signals.note: He will play a bit earlier but is not a major touch candidate while Irving is rolling.

signals.claim: McCollum will continue as a high-level starting outside corner.
signals.note: He is playing at an all-pro level with zero receptions allowed, which is good for the Bucs' defense and IDP/DST value.
signals.quote: Zion is playing like an all pro corner right now.

signals.claim: Parrish remains a starting outside corner, with occasional breathers when he tires.
signals.note: His deflections and coverage help the defense; he is a plus for IDP and DST.
signals.quote: parish has some great deflections there

signals.claim: Bain is back and playing at a good level despite some rust.
signals.note: His return adds to a pass rush that had its best pressure game of the year, which helps IDP and DST.
signals.quote: He looked good, got to knock the rust off some technique wise

signals.claim: Walker is part of a young edge group producing pressure.
signals.note: He generated pressure without sacks; the pass rush is trending up, a minor IDP positive.
signals.quote: I thought all those guys brought pressure.

topics.detail: Bowles said running the ball is "kind of who we are" and leads to complementary football, with a consistent commitment to the run in this game.
Offensive line penalties have been creeping up each week; Bowles said some were questionable but the team must be fundamentally sound, while praising the effort.
The Bucs won the turnover battle for the first time this season and did not turn the ball over offensively.
Bowles took full responsibility for going for a touchdown instead of kicking a field goal for a 17-point lead, saying he got greedy.
Bowles said leaders spoke in a Saturday meeting, the team played for each other for 60 minutes, and he feels they turned a corner for one game but have a lot to clean up.
